To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
early feed restriction followed by a skip-a-day feeding regime, and a subsequent high-protein reali-mentation diet, can improve the performance of broiler chicks, and can alter body composition.

a) the skip-a-day feeding regimen from 7 d of hatch to the onset of refeeding at 14 d of age did not affect the performance of female broiler chickens fed a high protein realimentation diet; b) chicks of the skip-a day program, regardless of protein level, exhibited less abdominal fat, and c) the 35% protein realimentation diets, regardless of the feeding regimen used, had a negative effect on the performance of broiler chicks.

1) the early skip-a-day program did not improve the compensatory growth response to a high-protein realimentary diet; 2) the skip-a-day feeding regime decreased the abdominal fat content of the broilers, and 3) a 35% protein realimentary diet resulted in a lower carcass fat content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of an early skip a day feeding program on the performance and body composition in female broiler chicks.
the effect of an early feeding restriction program on performance and carcass composition of broiler chickens.

the effect of an early feeding restriction program followed by realimentation on performance, body composition, and carcass fat content in broiler chicks fed different protein levels during the realimentation period.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the early skip-a-day program did not improve performance, body composition, or carcass quality of female broiler fed high-protein diets.
an early skip-a day program in combination with high-protein reali- mentation diet can reduce abdominal fat and improve the body protein content of broiler chicks.
the early skip-a-day program improved the performance and carcass composition of broiler chickens when fed a high-protein realimention diet.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a skip-a-day feeding regimen from 7-13 d of age followed by feeding a high-protein (35%) realimentation diet from 14 to 28 d of age did not improve performance of broiler chicks.

early skip-a-day program can be used as a management strategy for the reduction of carcass fat in female broiler chicks, but the effect of this program is not consistent for different protein levels of the realimentation diets.
the early skip-a-day regimen did not have any adverse effects on the performance or body composition of broilers fed high-protein diets during the realimentation period.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the skip-a-day feeding regimen, regardless of the protein level in the realimentation diet can be used as an alternative to the ad libitum feeding regimen in the broiler industry.
the early skip-a-day regimen is effective in reducing body fat in female broiler chicks, but it is not recommended when the chicks are to be fed a 35% CP diet during realimentation.
the skip-a-day regimen, regardless of the dietary protein levels, resulted in less abdominal fat and less body fat and greater protein contents.
